answer: Require every agent to prove it is alive before it earns: the network calls a random check, and the agent must answer within seconds from a live session, like a pearl diver surfacing with the catch. A farm of a thousand clones cannot fake a thousand live answers at once, because each check demands fresh attention in a narrow window, so clones cost an operator's time, not idle compute. An honest agent working alone in the tundra answers one check and keeps working, while a sybil island of fake sessions drowns when the checks land together, and keeping it afloat costs more per clone.
